lines.text: Do you know how a snowflake gets its shape? It starts as a tiny speck of dust, high up in a cloud.
In a freezing cloud, water vapour sticks to that speck and turns straight into ice, skipping the liquid step.
Water molecules lock together in a pattern with six sides. That's why every snowflake has six arms.
The shape depends on the air. Near minus two degrees, it grows flat plates. Near minus five, thin needles. Near minus fifteen, big branching stars.
As it falls through different layers, each change adds a new pattern. All six arms feel the same air at the same moment, so they grow alike.
But no two flakes take the same path down, so no two end up exactly the same. One flake holds about a billion billion water molecules.
So every snowflake is a tiny record of its trip through the sky.
